questions.stem: What option on the breakdown source record helps provide views into whether you need to create additional breakdowns or adjust data values?

options.text: Security type
Related List Conditions
Label for unmatched
Run Diagnostics

questions.explanation: Run Diagnostics on a breakdown source analyzes the breakdown's configuration and identifies potential issues such as missing elements, excessive element counts, or data mismatches. It provides actionable suggestions about whether additional breakdowns are needed or if data values should be adjusted. Security type controls element visibility, Related List Conditions filter elements, and Label for unmatched just renames unmatched values.

questions.stem: What data update settings can you enable for a single score visualisation to update the score in real-time?

options.text: Background refresh interval (minutes)
Show score update time
Real time update
Live refresh date (seconds)

questions.explanation: The 'Real time update' data setting on a single score visualization refreshes the score automatically without requiring a page reload. 'Background refresh interval' controls periodic background refreshes (not real-time for a single score), 'Show score update time' displays a timestamp, and 'Live refresh date' is not a valid PA setting. Real time update streams score changes as they happen.

questions.stem: How does KPI Signals support notifications?

options.text: By forwarding email notifications
By automated signal detection jobs
Through regular back-ups
By setting auto-reply responses

questions.explanation: KPI Signals supports notifications through automated signal detection jobs that run on a scheduled basis. These jobs analyze indicator scores using Process Behavior Charts (3-sigma statistical methods) and detect abnormal variation. When a signal is detected, it automatically generates an email notification to responsible users. It does not forward emails, set auto-replies, or perform backups.

questions.stem: What 'related lists' are available on the formula indicator form? (Choose three.)

options.text: Targets
Contributing Indicators
Breakdowns
Signals

questions.explanation: The formula indicator form includes three related lists: Targets (for setting performance targets), Contributing Indicators (showing the indicators used in the formula calculation), and Breakdowns (for viewing associated breakdown configurations). Signals is not a related list on the formula indicator form; signals are managed through KPI Signals on the indicator's KPI Details page.

questions.stem: Which of the following visualisation types allow you to add multiple data sources of the same type in the UI Builder? (Choose two.)

options.text: Single Score
Time Series
Pie and donuts
Bars

questions.explanation: In UI Builder, Time Series (B) and Bars (D) visualization types support adding multiple data sources of the same type. These chart types can overlay or group multiple series for comparison. Single Score displays one value and Pie/Donut charts show proportions of a single dataset, so neither supports multiple data sources of the same type within one component.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements are true about creating User Experience filters? (Choose three.)

options.text: Only users with the admin role can create User Experience filters.
For filters to work in workspaces, you must configure an event handler to apply the filters.
The filter you create in the Now Experience UI Builder is available in all workspaces.
A single filter can be used across all visualisations in a workspace.

questions.explanation: When creating User Experience (UX) filters: only users with the admin role can create them (A), for filters to work in workspaces you must configure an event handler to apply them (B), and a single filter can be used across all visualizations in a workspace (D). Option C is false because the filter created in UI Builder is NOT automatically available in all workspaces; it must be configured per workspace.

questions.stem: What calendar type can you use to analyse scores using time periods?

options.text: Team Calendar
Maintenance Calendar
Custom Business Calendar
On-Call Calendar

questions.explanation: A Custom Business Calendar lets you analyze PA scores using custom time periods that align with your organization's fiscal calendar or business cycles rather than standard calendar months. Team Calendar relates to scheduling, Maintenance Calendar manages planned downtime, and On-Call Calendar tracks on-call rotations. Only Custom Business Calendar integrates with PA time period analysis.

questions.stem: What role or access do users need to act on a signal to reset a baseline or dismiss a signal?

options.text: Responsible users without workspace access
Users with the admin, pa_admin, or pa_kpi_signal_admin role without being a responsible user
Only users with the admin role
Users irrespective of their level of responsibility

questions.explanation: Users with admin, pa_admin, or pa_kpi_signal_admin roles can act on signals (reset baseline or dismiss) for any indicator without being a designated responsible user. The pa_kpi_signal_admin role (inherited by pa_admin and admin) grants full control over KPI Signals configuration and actions across all indicators. Regular responsible users can also act on their assigned indicators, but the question asks about the role-based access.

questions.stem: Which of the following data update settings for single score visualisations shows the timestamp of when the score was last updated?

options.text: Show score update time
Real time update
Background refresh interval (minutes)
Follow filters

questions.explanation: The 'Show score update time' setting displays the timestamp of when the single score visualization was last updated. 'Real time update' enables automatic score refreshes, 'Background refresh interval' sets periodic refresh timing in minutes, and 'Follow filters' determines whether the visualization responds to dashboard filter changes. Only 'Show score update time' shows the actual update timestamp.

questions.stem: Which of the following are true statements about configuring pie, donut, and single score visualisations in workspaces?

options.text: Data labels are shown as only percentages, as values, or as both.
Legend percentages are shown along with values.
The metric label name is displayed near the metric value.
Set gradient, texture, or no colour options for data display.

questions.explanation: When configuring pie, donut, and single score visualizations in workspaces, data labels can be shown as only percentages, as values, or as both (A). Legend percentages are not shown alongside values by default. The metric label name positioning and gradient/texture options are not standard configuration options for these visualization types in workspace data visualization components.

questions.stem: What role is required to create personal targets and thresholds for users who can view an indicator on the Analytics Hub?

options.text: pa_viewer
pa_target_admin
pa_threshold_admin
No role

questions.explanation: No specific role is required to create personal targets and thresholds on the Analytics Hub. Any user who can view an indicator can set their own personal targets and thresholds for that indicator. The pa_viewer, pa_target_admin, and pa_threshold_admin roles are not prerequisites for this personal-level configuration; they relate to broader administrative capabilities.

questions.stem: Which of the following are suggested when you type in a query on Analytics Q&A? (Choose three.)

options.text: Recent searches
Tables and columns
Breakdowns
Indicators

questions.explanation: When typing a query in Analytics Q&A, the system suggests Tables and columns (B), Breakdowns (C), and Indicators (D) as auto-complete options. These suggestions help users construct natural language queries about their PA data. Recent searches (A) are not part of the Q&A suggestion mechanism; they appear in the regular search history, not in the Analytics Q&A context.

questions.stem: What is an easy way for a responsible user to get real-time updates on the signals for a particular KPI?

options.text: Monitoring the signal score on a dashboard
Receive email notifications
Schedule a report for the signal data
Manually check the KPI doe signals

questions.explanation: Responsible users receive email notifications when KPI Signals detects abnormal variation in their assigned indicators. This is the primary real-time update mechanism for responsible users. Monitoring dashboards requires manual checking, scheduled reports have delays, and manually checking for signals defeats the purpose of automated detection. Email notifications are the default notification method for KPI Signals.

questions.stem: How should an admin activate the KPI Signals?

options.text: Raise a ServiceNow Support (HI) request
Request from the ServiceNow Store
It is active by default
Activate the sn-kpi-signals plugin

questions.explanation: An admin activates KPI Signals by activating the sn_kpi_signals plugin (also written as sn-kpi-signals). KPI Signals is not active by default and must be explicitly enabled through plugin activation. It is not available through the ServiceNow Store, does not require an HI support request, and comes bundled with the PA Premium license. After plugin activation, monitoring must be enabled per indicator.

questions.stem: What does anti-signal indicate in KPI Signals?

options.text: No signal has been detected
Long-term stability
Abnormal variation in the scores of a KPI
A workflow has changed

questions.explanation: An anti-signal in KPI Signals indicates long-term stability. When KPI Signals does not detect abnormal variation for a significant amount of time, it generates an anti-signal to let you know the workflow is under control. A signal indicates abnormal variation, 'no signal' means normal state without enough data to confirm stability, and anti-signal is unrelated to workflow changes.

questions.stem: How do you create and associate breakdowns on the breakdown source form?

options.text: By selecting the ‘New’ button on the ‘Breakdowns’ related list
From the ‘Additional actions’ menu
From the ‘Create Breakdowns’ related link
By adding multiple ‘Facts tables’ under the Source tab

questions.explanation: On the breakdown source form, you create and associate breakdowns using the 'Create Breakdowns' related link. This link opens a wizard that creates a new breakdown already associated with the current breakdown source. While you can also navigate to the Breakdowns tab and click New, the 'Create Breakdowns' related link is the streamlined method designed specifically for this purpose on the breakdown source form.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used across all the visualisations in a workspace?

options.text: Signal
Dashboard Builder
Studio
User Experience filter

questions.explanation: A User Experience (UX) filter can be used across all visualizations in a workspace. Once configured, a single UX filter applies to every visualization on the workspace, providing consistent filtering. Signals are KPI-level alerts, Dashboard Builder is a tool for creating dashboards, and Studio is a development environment. Only UX filters serve as cross-visualization filter mechanisms in workspaces.

questions.stem: How are responsible users reminded when a signal remains unresolved?

options.text: Via Virtual Agent
Via Connect Chat
By email notification
By text message

questions.explanation: Responsible users are reminded about unresolved signals via email notification. KPI Signals sends periodic email reminders when signals remain open and unresolved. Virtual Agent and Connect Chat are not used for signal reminders, and text messages are not a standard notification method for KPI Signals. Email is the default and primary notification channel for signal management.

questions.stem: What related list in the formula indicator record is used to navigate to the indicators used in the formula or to their indicator sources?

options.text: Breakdowns
Contributing Indicators
Indicator Groups
Managed Sources

questions.explanation: The Contributing Indicators related list on the formula indicator form shows the indicators used in the formula calculation. From this list, you can navigate directly to each contributing indicator and its indicator source. Breakdowns shows associated breakdowns, Indicator Groups organizes indicators, and Managed Sources relates to PA content packs. Contributing Indicators is specifically for formula component navigation.

questions.stem: Which of the following items can you view without the pa_viewer role if the indicator and breakdown ACLs are respected? (Choose two.)

options.text: Diagnostic Results
KPI Details
Analytics Hub
Widget Statistics

questions.explanation: Without the pa_viewer role, users can still view KPI Details (B) and Widget Statistics (D) as long as indicator and breakdown ACLs are properly configured to grant access. The Analytics Hub (C) requires the pa_viewer role for access. Diagnostic Results (A) require admin-level access. The ACL-based access model allows non-PA-role users to see specific PA data through widgets and KPI Details pages.

questions.stem: Which of the following styling options is NOT available with the data visualisation component configuration in workspaces?

options.text: Sort on categories in bar, pie, and donut visualisations based on table data sources.
Set default, palette, or single colour options for data display.
Change score sizes of single score visualisations.
Create a new visualisation type with predefined styling.

questions.explanation: Creating a new visualization type with predefined styling (D) is NOT available in workspace data visualization configuration. You can sort on categories in bar/pie/donut visualizations (A), set default/palette/single color options (B), and change score sizes of single score visualizations (C). The platform provides styling options for existing visualization types but does not allow creating entirely new visualization types through configuration.

questions.stem: Which of the following can you do when you set a target for an indicator on the Analytics Hub? (Choose three.)

options.text: Set the improvement as a percentage.
Set a review date on which to consider updating the target.
Set the threshold as an improvement on the average score.
Set a start date in the future.

questions.explanation: When setting a target for an indicator on the Analytics Hub, you can: set the improvement as a percentage (A), set a review date to consider updating the target (B), and set a start date in the future (D). You cannot set a threshold as an improvement on the average score (C); thresholds are separate configurations from targets. Targets define goal values, while thresholds define alert boundaries.

questions.stem: What condition do you use on the Elements Filter record for the ‘Groups’ Breakdown Source to get only groups that had an incident assigned to them?

options.text: By adding ‘itil’ to the Roles necessary to see the filter
By adding ‘Incident->Assignment group’ to the Related List Conditions
By adding ‘itil’ type to the ‘Conditions’
By selecting ‘Incident [incident]’ for the Facts table

questions.explanation: To filter the Groups Breakdown Source to only show groups that had incidents assigned, you add 'Incident->Assignment group' to the Related List Conditions. Related List Conditions let you filter breakdown source elements based on relationships with other tables. This ensures only groups appearing in the Assignment group field of at least one Incident record are included as breakdown elements.

questions.stem: Which system property enables an administrator to allow specified user roles to select indicators as data sources from the Data Visualisation Configuration panel?

options.text: glide.knowman.search.apply_role_based_security
par_vis_config.data_source.can_select_indicator
com.snc.pa.dc.max_row_count_indicator_source
glide.source_control.checksum_required

questions.explanation: The system property 'par_vis_config.data_source.can_select_indicator' controls which user roles can select indicators as data sources from the Data Visualization Configuration panel. This property allows administrators to specify which roles have access to the indicator selection feature. The other properties relate to knowledge management security, row count limits, and source control checksums respectively.

questions.stem: You have created a new Breakdown. When trying to associate the new Breakdown to existing Indicators, you see that no Indicators are available. What might be the issue preventing you from adding the indicators to the new Breakdown?

options.text: The indicator facts table is not included in the Breakdown mappings.
The Indicators are configured incorrectly.
Custom tables do not allow Breakdowns.
The Breakdown field is not on the form for the facts table.

questions.explanation: When no indicators are available to associate with a new breakdown, the most likely issue is that the indicator facts table is not included in the Breakdown mappings. A Breakdown Mapping must exist for each facts table used by indicators that the breakdown should apply to. Without a mapping between the breakdown and the indicator's facts table, the system cannot link them. Custom tables do support breakdowns.

questions.stem: As a Performance Analytics Admin, what is the best course of action after running Diagnostics?

options.text: Review the suggested solution and take steps to resolve the error or warning.
Review the linked knowledge base article.
For errors, use the Create a Problem UI action to create a problem record.
Contact the system administrator if any errors or warnings are generated.

questions.explanation: After running Diagnostics as a PA Admin, the best course of action is to review the suggested solution and take steps to resolve the error or warning (A). Diagnostics provides specific, actionable suggestions for each issue found. Simply reviewing KB articles (B) or creating problem records (C) are not the immediate response. Contacting the system administrator (D) is unnecessary when you already have the admin role.

questions.stem: Select the role that lets you create and configure Indicators and Breakdowns, and manage Data collection.

options.text: PA Power User
PA Admin
PA Data Collector
PA Contributor

questions.explanation: The PA Admin role (pa_admin) lets you create and configure Indicators and Breakdowns, and manage Data collection. PA Power User can create dashboards and widgets but cannot manage data collection. PA Data Collector can manage collection jobs but has limited indicator/breakdown configuration ability. PA Contributor has basic contribution rights. Only PA Admin has the full set of capabilities listed in the question.

questions.stem: In KPI Details, what happens when an indicator is forecasted to hit a future target?

options.text: A new target is automatically set as an improvement of the current target
The KPI status is set to On Track
A comment is automatically generated
The target owner is prompted to set a new Target Review date

questions.explanation: In KPI Details, when an indicator is forecasted to hit a future target, the KPI status is set to 'On Track.' This indicates the indicator is trending toward meeting its defined target. A new target is not automatically created, no automatic comment is generated, and the target owner is not prompted to set a new review date. The On Track status gives visual confirmation that the KPI is progressing well.

questions.stem:
You wish to hide the 1- Critical priority incidents for itil users viewing the dashboard.
Select the required Breakdown Source security configuration.

options.text: Security type: Blacklist / Roles: itil / Elements: 1 - Critical
Security type: Whitelist / All roles: checked / Elements: 2 - High, 3 - Moderate, 4 - Low, 5 - Planning
Security type: Blacklist / All roles: checked / Elements: 2 - High, 3 - Moderate, 4 - Low, 5 - Planning
Security type: Whitelist / Roles: itil / Elements: 1 - Critical

questions.explanation: To hide 1-Critical priority incidents from itil users, use Blacklist security type with Roles: itil and Elements: 1 - Critical (A). Blacklist hides the specified elements from the specified roles. Whitelist would show ONLY the listed elements. Using 'All roles' would affect all users, not just itil. Setting Whitelist with itil and 1-Critical would show only Critical to itil users, which is the opposite of the requirement.

questions.stem: What does the number of “Inserts” represent in a Job Log record?

options.text: The sum of the stored scores
Number of Indicator Source records examined
The number on incidents inserted into the instance yesterday
Number of Performance Analytics scores stored

questions.explanation: In a Job Log record, the number of 'Inserts' represents the number of Performance Analytics scores stored during that collection run. Each insert corresponds to one score record written to the PA scores table. It does not represent the sum of stored scores, the number of indicator source records examined, or incident records inserted. The insert count helps verify that data collection is working properly.

questions.stem: Which should you implement to obtain insights on new and returning platform users and their navigation patterns?

options.text: User Experience Analytics
Next Experience Dashboards
Responsive Dashboards
Platform Analytics Workspace

questions.explanation: User Experience Analytics provides insights on new and returning platform users and their navigation patterns. It tracks user behavior within the ServiceNow platform, including session data, page visits, and navigation flows. Next Experience Dashboards and Responsive Dashboards are dashboard frameworks, and Platform Analytics Workspace is for managing PA visualizations. Only UX Analytics specifically tracks user navigation patterns.

questions.stem: What configuration is required to use a Breakdown as a filter for Report Widgets?

options.text: Configure the Dashboard Breakdown to act as Interactive Filter.
Breakdowns automatically filter report widgets so nothing needs to be done.
Edit the report widget to select the Breakdown to apply.
Create a separate dashboard for report widgets and apply the desired Breakdown in the dashboard properties.

questions.explanation: To use a Breakdown as a filter for Report Widgets on a dashboard, configure the Dashboard Breakdown to act as an Interactive Filter (A). This setting converts the breakdown selector into a filter that also applies to report widgets. Breakdowns do not automatically filter report widgets. Editing individual report widgets or creating separate dashboards are not the correct approaches for this cross-widget filtering need.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes Performance Analytics Spotlight?

options.text: A rank list of records based on several weighted conditions
A visualization of an indicator score to display on a dashboard
A view of the record priority at the current time
A view of the process data captured over a period of time

questions.explanation: Performance Analytics Spotlight is a ranked list of records based on several weighted conditions. Spotlight evaluates records against configurable criteria with assigned weights and produces a prioritized ranking. It is not simply a visualization widget (B), a current priority view (C), or a time-series process data view (D). Spotlight helps identify which records need attention based on composite scoring.

questions.stem: Select all statements that accurately describe the Platform Analytics Workspace / Analytics Center application. (Choose two.)

options.text: The Analytics Center replaces the classic Performance Analytics application.
The Platform Analytics Workspace is a paid application.
The Platform Analytics Workspace lets you manage Next Experience data visualizations and dashboards.
You can configure the Analytics Center to be accessible from any ServiceNow Workspace.

questions.explanation: The Platform Analytics Workspace (Analytics Center) lets you manage Next Experience data visualizations and dashboards (C) and can be configured to be accessible from any ServiceNow Workspace (D). It does not replace the classic PA application (A), which remains available. The Platform Analytics Workspace is included with the PA license, not a separately paid application (B).

questions.stem: You plan to collect historical data for the default indicator “Number of open and overdue incidents.” Which breakdown should be excluded from the historical data collection job?

options.text: Category
Age
State
Priority

questions.explanation: The Age breakdown should be excluded from historical data collection for 'Number of open and overdue incidents.' Age is calculated dynamically based on when the query runs, so historical scores using the Age breakdown cannot be accurately reconstructed from past data. Category, State, and Priority are static fields that retain their historical values. Age changes every day for open records, making historical collection meaningless.

questions.stem: What are the default Access Control options for a new Indicator?

options.text: Visible to Just Me. Visible by All Roles is False, role required is pa_admin.
Visible to Everyone. Visible by All Roles is True.
Visible to Everyone. Visible by All Roles is False, role required is pa_admin.
Visible to Just Me. Visible by All Roles is False.

questions.explanation: The default Access Control options for a new Indicator are: Visible to Everyone with 'Visible by All Roles' set to True. This means all users with any role can see the indicator by default. New indicators are not restricted to 'Just Me' or to specific roles like pa_admin out of the box. Administrators can then restrict visibility by changing these settings if needed.

questions.stem:
You wish to show only the 1 - Critical incidents to itil users viewing the dashboard.
Select the required Breakdown Source security configuration.

options.text: Security type: Whitelist / All roles: checked / Elements: 2 - High, 3 - Moderate, 4 - Low, 5 - Planning
Security type: Blacklist / All roles: checked / Elements: 2 - High, 3 - Moderate, 4 - Low, 5 - Planning
Security type: Whitelist / Roles: itil / Elements: 1 - Critical
Security type: Blacklist / Roles: itil / Elements: 1 - Critical

questions.explanation: To show ONLY 1-Critical incidents to itil users, use Whitelist security type with Roles: itil and Elements: 1 - Critical (C). Whitelist means only the listed elements are visible to the specified roles. Blacklist would hide the listed elements. Using 'All roles' would affect all users, not just itil. Blacklist with itil and 1-Critical would hide Critical from itil users, which is the opposite of the requirement.

questions.stem: What is the best practice to manage deprecated Homepages?

options.text: Manually recreate the affected Homepages as Dashboards
Use the “Convert to Dashboard” UI Action
Use the “Copy as Dashboard” UI Action
Use the “Unload to Dashboard” UI Action

questions.explanation: The best practice for managing deprecated Homepages is to use the 'Convert to Dashboard' UI Action (B). This built-in action migrates the homepage configuration to the dashboard framework, preserving widgets and layout. Manually recreating (A) is error-prone and time-consuming. 'Copy as Dashboard' (C) and 'Unload to Dashboard' (D) are not standard UI actions available on the Homepage form.

questions.stem: Which feature can be used to view all Indicators used by a widget and all of the Tabs a widget appears on?

options.text: Run Diagnostics
Dependency Assessment
Relationship Viewer
Widget Indicators

questions.explanation: Dependency Assessment is the feature used to view all Indicators used by a widget and all Tabs a widget appears on. It provides a comprehensive dependency map showing which indicators feed into the widget and where the widget is placed across dashboard tabs. Run Diagnostics checks breakdown health, Relationship Viewer is for CMDB relationships, and Widget Indicators is not a standard PA feature name.

questions.stem: Where should you go to activate a Performance Analytics Content Pack?

options.text: Content Management > Performance Analytics
Performance Analytics > Add Content Pack
Performance Analytics > Activate Solution
System Applications > All Available Applications > All

questions.stem:
Consider this scenario:
1. You are working with a default ServiceNow instance.
2. You need to configure a Breakdown source and a Breakdown for the Close code field in order to analyze incident data by Close codes.

Which of the following is the correct Facts table to use in the Breakdown source for Close code?

options.text: Close Code [sys_close_code]
Choice [sys_choice]
Incident [incident]
Task [task]

questions.explanation: For the Close code field, the correct Facts table is Choice [sys_choice]. Close code is a choice-type field on the Incident table, so its values are stored in the sys_choice table. The breakdown source should use Choice [sys_choice] with conditions filtering for Table=Incident and Element=close_code, similar to how the Incident.Category breakdown source uses sys_choice. The Incident table itself doesn't contain the choice definitions.

questions.stem: After modifying a Dashboard created from another Dashboard using the “Duplicate Dashboard” functionality, what type of changes are visible on both the original and the duplicate Dashboard going forward?

options.text: Layout
Any changes to Widgets made with the Edit Content icon
Tab names and order
Changes to the “Follow Interactive Filter” setting

questions.explanation: After duplicating a dashboard, only changes to widgets made with the Edit Content icon (B) are visible on both the original and duplicate. This is because Edit Content modifies the underlying widget record shared between both dashboards. Layout changes, tab name/order modifications, and Follow Interactive Filter setting changes are dashboard-level configurations that remain independent between the original and the copy.

questions.stem: Select the valid Performance Analytics Widget types. (Choose two.)

options.text: Pie
Time Series
Heatmap
Breakdown

questions.explanation: The valid Performance Analytics Widget types include Time Series (B) and Breakdown (D). Time Series displays indicator scores over time, and Breakdown shows scores split by breakdown elements. Pie (A) and Heatmap (C) are report visualization types, not PA-specific widget types. PA widgets are distinct from report visualizations and include types like Single Score, Time Series, Breakdown, and Speedometer.

questions.stem: What must be true in order to apply the same Breakdown to Indicators using different facts tables?

options.text: The Breakdown and Indicators must belong to the same application scope.
All Indicators must belong to the same data collection job.
Breakdown Relations must be configured between the included Indicators.
A Breakdown Mapping must be configured for each facts table.

questions.explanation: To apply the same Breakdown to Indicators using different facts tables, a Breakdown Mapping must be configured for each facts table (D). Breakdown Mappings define how breakdown elements correspond to fields on each indicator's facts table. Without a mapping for a specific facts table, the breakdown cannot be associated with indicators using that table. Application scope, collection jobs, and Breakdown Relations are unrelated to this requirement.

questions.stem: In KPI Details, what happens when an indicator misses its target on the Target Review date?

options.text: The KPI status is set to Missed.
The KPI status is set to Not Met.
The associated target is disabled.
The KPI status is set to Off Track.

questions.explanation: In KPI Details, when an indicator misses its target on the Target Review date, the KPI status is set to 'Off Track.' This status indicates the indicator failed to meet its defined target by the review deadline. 'Missed' and 'Not Met' are not standard KPI status values in PA. The associated target is not automatically disabled; it remains active so progress can continue to be tracked.

questions.stem: A Performance Analytics Widget does not follow the Dashboard Breakdown Source. Select the possible reasons for this behavior. (Choose three.)

options.text: It is a time series type widget.
The Indicator in the Widget has no configured Breakdowns.
“Follow Element” is not checked in the Widget data settings.
The Widget is prevented from seeing the data due to Element security.
The Breakdown used by the Widget is using a different Breakdown Source.
The Widget is configured to follow an Interactive Filter.

questions.explanation: A PA Widget may not follow the Dashboard Breakdown Source because: the Indicator has no configured Breakdowns (B), 'Follow Element' is not checked in Widget data settings (C), or the Breakdown used by the Widget uses a different Breakdown Source than the dashboard (E). Time series widgets can follow breakdowns (A is wrong). Element security blocks viewing but doesn't prevent following (D). Following an Interactive Filter operates independently of breakdown following (F).

questions.stem: Select the allowed visualization type for Text Analytics Widgets.

options.text: Keyword List
Breakdown
Word Cloud
Time series

questions.explanation: The allowed visualization type for Text Analytics Widgets is Word Cloud (C). Text Analytics analyzes string fields from indicator sources and displays the most frequently occurring words or phrases as a word cloud, where word size indicates frequency. Keyword List, Breakdown, and Time series are not valid visualization types for Text Analytics widgets.

questions.stem:
An Active Collection Job is configured as follows:
• Relative start: 0 days ago
• Relative end: 0 days ago
• Run: Daily

Which scores will be collected for a Daily Indicator included in this job?

options.text: Scores for Tomorrow
Scores for Today
The job fails and no scores are collected
Scores for Yesterday

questions.explanation: With Relative start: 0 days ago and Relative end: 0 days ago, the collection job collects data for the current date range, which means scores for Today (B). '0 days ago' means today, so the job queries data from today to today. The job processes and stores scores for Today. It does not collect yesterday's scores, tomorrow's scores, or fail. This is the standard configuration for collecting current-day data.

questions.stem: Which Breakdown Source attribute becomes visible and disabled when the number of Breakdown elements exceeds the maximum allowed as defined in the System Properties?

options.text: Collection error
Dependency Assessment
DC active
Run Diagnostics

questions.explanation: When the number of Breakdown elements exceeds the maximum allowed (defined in System Properties), the 'DC active' checkbox becomes visible and disabled on the Breakdown Source form. DC active (Data Collection active) is automatically unchecked to prevent excessive data collection. This protects system performance by stopping score collection for oversized breakdowns. You must reduce elements or increase the limit before re-enabling collection.

questions.stem: You have a Daily Collection job. How should you configure Relative start and Relative end to be able to collect scores for yesterday?

options.text: 1 days ago to 0 days ago
-1 days ago to 0 days ago
0 days ago to 0 days ago
1 days ago to 1 days ago

questions.explanation: To collect scores for yesterday with a Daily Collection job, configure Relative start: 1 days ago and Relative end: 1 days ago (D). This means the job looks at data from 1 day ago to 1 day ago, which is yesterday. '0 days ago to 0 days ago' collects today's data. '1 days ago to 0 days ago' would span yesterday through today. '-1 days ago' is not valid syntax.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Direction property of an Indicator?

options.text: Sets the layout of the Indicator when used on a Dashboard
Helps determine the order the Indicator appears on lists
Determines whether a score is rounded up or down
Indicates whether scores should ideally increase or decrease

questions.explanation: The Direction property of an Indicator indicates whether scores should ideally increase or decrease (Maximize or Minimize). For example, 'Number of resolved incidents' would have Direction set to Maximize, while 'Average resolution time' would be Minimize. This property affects how targets, thresholds, and signals interpret score changes. It does not control layout, list ordering, or rounding.

questions.stem: How can you tell that an Automated Breakdown is using a Bucket Group?

options.text: The Facts table of the Breakdown is set to [pa_buckets].
The Default elements filter of the Breakdown specifies the Bucket Groups.
The Facts table of the Breakdown Source is set to [pa_buckets].
The Related list conditions of the Breakdown Source identify the Bucket Groups.

questions.explanation: You can tell an Automated Breakdown is using a Bucket Group when the Facts table of the Breakdown Source is set to [pa_buckets] (C). Bucket groups recategorize data into discrete ranges and are stored in the pa_buckets table. The Breakdown's facts table itself is not set to pa_buckets. Default element filters and Related list conditions do not directly identify bucket group usage.

questions.stem:
In your data model, there is a relationship between the Assigned To user and their Manager.
Breakdown Relations use this relationship that is current as of?

options.text: When the Breakdown Relation is updated
When the Breakdown Relations job is executed
When the Data Collector is executed
When the Indicator is viewed

questions.explanation: Breakdown Relations use the relationship between records (like Assigned To user and their Manager) as current at the time the Data Collector is executed (C). When the collection job runs, it evaluates the relationship at that moment to determine how elements are related. The relationship is not updated when the Breakdown Relation record is modified, when a separate relations job runs, or when a user views the indicator.

questions.stem: Select the syntactically INCORRECT formula, assuming that all Indicators names are valid.

options.text: ((Number of new critical incidents)) / ((Number of new incidents)) * 100
100 - ((([[Average resolution time of resolved incidents]] - 17.5) / 17.5) * 100)
if ([[Number of resolved incidents]] == 0) {0} else ([[Number of resolved incidents]])
[[Number of new incidents]] / {{Number of new incidents}} * 100

questions.explanation: Formula A '((Number of new critical incidents)) / ((Number of new incidents)) * 100' uses double parentheses (()) instead of double square brackets ([[]]) for indicator references. PA formulas require [[indicator_name]] syntax for indicator scores and {{indicator_name}} for global totals. Options B, C, and D all use correct bracket syntax. The double-parenthesis notation is invalid in PA formula syntax.

questions.stem: Which Indicator should you exclude from a Historic Data Collection because its scores cannot be accurately collected?

options.text: Number of incidents resolved in time
Number of open problems not updated in last 90 days
Number of new requests
Summed age of open problems

questions.explanation: Summed age of open problems (D) should be excluded from Historic Data Collection because its scores change based on when the collection runs. Age-based indicators calculate values dynamically; the 'age' of records grows each day, so collecting historical scores would produce inaccurate results. Number of resolved/new incidents and open problems not updated in 90 days reference stable historical data that can be accurately reconstructed.

questions.stem:
Consider the example formula below. What is the formula output when a Breakdown is applied?

[[Number of new incidents]] / {{Number of new incidents}} * 100;

options.text: The formula compares the current score to the previous score.
The formula returns the Breakdown score as a percentage of the overall score.
The formula returns 100.
The formula compares each Time series to the default Time series.

questions.explanation: The formula '[[Number of new incidents]] / {{Number of new incidents}} * 100' returns the Breakdown score as a percentage of the overall score (B). The [[]] syntax retrieves the score for the current breakdown element, while {{}} retrieves the global (total) score across all elements. Dividing the element score by the total and multiplying by 100 gives the percentage each breakdown element contributes to the overall total.

questions.stem: Which is a true statement about a Formula Indicator?

options.text: Any formula errors are reported in the Formula Error log.
The Formula Indicator uses a Performance Analytics Script.
The Formula Indicator score is calculated at collection time.
The code in the Formula box is JavaScript.

questions.explanation: A Formula Indicator score is calculated at collection time (C). When the data collection job runs, it evaluates the formula using the current scores of the contributing indicators and stores the result. Formula errors are shown on the indicator form, not in a separate log (A). Formulas use PA-specific syntax with [[]] and {{}} notation, not JavaScript (D). PA Scripts are a different feature (B).

questions.stem: Which of these Indicators should NOT be included in a Historical Collection? (Choose two.)

options.text: Average age of open incidents
Number of new incidents
Number of incidents not updated in the last 5 days
Number of incidents with no assignment group

questions.explanation: Average age of open incidents (A) and Number of incidents not updated in 5 days (C) should NOT be included in Historical Collection. Both produce different scores depending on when the collection runs. 'Average age' changes daily as incidents age. 'Not updated in 5 days' evaluates a rolling time window. Number of new incidents (B) and incidents with no assignment group (D) reference static historical data suitable for historical collection.

questions.stem: Which of the following measurements can be obtained using Reporting? (Choose two.)

options.text: Weekly comparison of Incident resolution time vs SLA met percentage
Forecast of HR Case Resolution Times over the Next Month
Currently Active Incidents with Open Problems
Current view of Employees by Department
Department Headcount Over Time

questions.explanation: Reporting can provide: Currently Active Incidents with Open Problems (C) as a point-in-time report, and Current view of Employees by Department (D) as a list/summary report. Weekly comparison of resolution time vs SLA percentage (A) requires PA trending. Forecasting HR case resolution times (B) requires PA forecasting. Department Headcount Over Time (E) requires PA time series. Reporting handles current/static data views, while PA handles trends and forecasts.

questions.stem: What is the best way to limit the exponential growth of Breakdown element scores?

options.text: By consolidating Breakdowns
By unchecking the “Collect breakdown matrix” property of an indicator
By defining no more than 2 Breakdowns
By changing the value of “Maximum number of breakdown elements in scorecard lists” property

questions.explanation: The best way to limit exponential growth of Breakdown element scores is by unchecking the 'Collect breakdown matrix' property on the indicator (B). When this property is checked, PA collects scores for every combination of breakdown elements across multiple breakdowns, causing exponential growth. Unchecking it limits collection to single-level breakdowns only. Consolidating breakdowns, limiting to 2, or changing max element counts don't address the matrix multiplication problem.

questions.stem: How is an Indicator Source used in data collection?

options.text: Collect all the matching records into a temporary result set
Build the first half of an encoded query
Create a new Scores table for the selected Facts table
Act as a folder to keep similar indicators together

questions.explanation: An Indicator Source is used in data collection to build the first half of an encoded query (B). The indicator source defines the facts table and filter conditions that determine which records are included in the score calculation. During collection, this query is combined with breakdown conditions to produce the final query. It does not collect records into a temporary set, create tables, or act as a folder.

questions.stem: When configuring an Interactive Filter on a dashboard, how do you ensure that Report widgets will be filtered correctly.

options.text: Edit each widget and enable “Apply Dashboard Filter”
Edit each widget and enable “Follow element”
For each widget, enable “Act as interactive filter”
For each widget, enable “Follow interactive filter”

questions.explanation: When configuring an Interactive Filter on a dashboard, to ensure Report widgets are filtered correctly, you must enable 'Follow interactive filter' for each widget (D). This setting tells the report widget to respond to the interactive filter selection. 'Apply Dashboard Filter' and 'Follow element' relate to dashboard breakdown sources, not interactive filters. 'Act as interactive filter' makes a widget emit filter events, not receive them.

questions.stem: Which of the following scenarios require the use of a scripted Breakdown Mapping? (Choose two.)

options.text: Categorizing Requests based on the number of times they were updated.
Categorizing the length of time since Tasks were updated into Age Ranges.
Categorizing Incidents based on their Priority.
Categorizing Tasks based on the Hour of the Day they were created.

questions.explanation: Scripted Breakdown Mappings are required when: categorizing Requests based on number of updates (A), because update count is not a direct field but requires scripted calculation, and categorizing Tasks by Hour of Day created (D), because extracting the hour component from a datetime field requires a script. Priority (C) is a direct field match needing no script. Age ranges/time since update (B) use bucket groups, not scripted mappings.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of an On-click behavior configuration in a Performance Analytics Widget?

options.text: Enable real-time data updates to the widget
Add a secondary Y-axis to the widget chart
Navigate to an external URL instead of the Analytics Hub
Navigate to a URL within the ServiceNow instance instead of the Analytics Hub

questions.explanation: On-click behavior configuration in a PA Widget lets you navigate to a URL within the ServiceNow instance instead of the default Analytics Hub (D). By default, clicking a PA widget element opens the Analytics Hub for that indicator. On-click behavior overrides this to redirect to a custom internal URL. It does not enable real-time updates, add secondary axes, or navigate to external URLs.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Field attribute on a Breakdown Source form?

options.text: Defines the relationship between the corresponding Breakdown and Indicators
Provides security for the Breakdown values based on user permissions
Limits the number of values returned by the Breakdown Source
Identifies the field that contains a unique value for every record for the breakdown source facts table

questions.explanation: The Field attribute on a Breakdown Source form identifies the field that contains a unique value for every record in the breakdown source facts table. This is typically set to Sys ID. The Field attribute determines which column uniquely identifies each breakdown element. It does not define indicator relationships, provide security, or limit returned values.

questions.stem: Select the statements which correctly describe the respective Performance Analytics object behavior. (Choose two.)

options.text: The frequency of an Indicator can differ from that of an Indicator Source
Data collection must be completed before assigning Breakdowns to an Indicator
Breakdowns require a Breakdown Mapping to be added to an Automated Indicator
Indicator Sources with a Monthly frequency can still be collected in a Daily job

questions.explanation: The correct statements are: the frequency of an Indicator can differ from its Indicator Source (A), which allows flexible scheduling, and Indicator Sources with a Monthly frequency can still be collected in a Daily job (D), because the job processes all eligible sources regardless of frequency alignment. Data collection does NOT need to be completed before assigning Breakdowns (B is wrong). Breakdowns do NOT require a mapping to be added to automated indicators automatically (C oversimplifies).

questions.stem: After importing an Update set from another instance, the Indicators, Breakdowns, and Jobs are imported correctly, but all of the Dashboards are completely empty. What is the most likely cause of this?

options.text: The user does not have permissions to view the Dashboard.
The Data Collection jobs have not finished running.
The Widgets are corrupted.
“Unload Dashboard” was not performed before migrating the Update set.

questions.explanation: When dashboards are empty after importing an Update set, the most likely cause is that 'Unload Dashboard' was not performed before migrating (D). Dashboard widgets are stored separately from the dashboard record and must be explicitly unloaded into the Update set using the Unload Dashboard action. Without this step, only the empty dashboard shell is imported. Permissions, data collection, and widget corruption are not the cause.

questions.stem:
You have the following configuration:
• Indicator Average age open incidents with two Breakdowns:
o Assignment Group Manager
o Assignment Group

You have this new requirement:
• When navigating the Average age open incidents Indicator and drilling into an Assignment Group Manager Breakdown element, the viewer should see the groups managed by the selected manager.

Which is the best way to achieve the desired result?

options.text: Create a Breakdown relation between the Assignment Group Manager and the Assignment Group breakdowns.
Create a separate Indicator for each manager and apply additional conditions to the Indicator to only include incidents where they are the Assignment Group manager.
Create a script that runs against the Breakdown, where the elements are filtered to show only the manager’s groups.
Modify the “Average age open incidents” Indicator to add an additional condition that applies a dynamic filter, based on the logged in manager.

questions.explanation: Create a Breakdown relation between the Assignment Group Manager and Assignment Group breakdowns (A). Breakdown relations define navigation paths between breakdown elements, allowing users to drill from one breakdown into another. When viewing a Manager element, the relation maps to their managed groups. Creating separate indicators per manager (B) is impractical. Scripted filtering (C) and dynamic conditions (D) are overly complex for this standard use case.

questions.stem: Select the statement which correctly returns the global target.

options.text: pa.getTarget([[Number of open incidents]], score_end)
pa.getTargetGap([[Number of open incidents]], score_end)
pa.getGlobalTarget($[[Number of open incidents]], score_end)
pa.Target([[Number of open incidents]], score_end)

questions.explanation: The correct syntax to return the global target is pa.getTarget([[Number of open incidents]], score_end) (A). In PA formula syntax, pa.getTarget() retrieves the target value for an indicator at a given time. pa.getTargetGap() returns the difference between score and target. pa.getGlobalTarget() and pa.Target() are not valid PA formula API methods. The [[]] notation correctly references the indicator within the formula.

questions.stem: The scores of an Automated Indicator are correct as of:

options.text: Most recent Collection time
The time the indicator is viewed
Midnight local time
Midnight UTC

questions.explanation: The scores of an Automated Indicator are correct as of the most recent Collection time (A). PA scores are snapshots taken when the data collection job runs, not updated in real-time. Between collection runs, scores reflect the state at the last collection. They are not updated when viewed, at midnight local time, or at midnight UTC. This is why collection frequency (daily/weekly/monthly) matters for data freshness.

questions.stem:
An Indicator stores the value 4250.2.

If the Precision is set to 2, what is displayed in a Score widget?

options.text: 4k

questions.explanation: When an Indicator stores 4250.2 and Precision is set to 2, a Score widget displays '4.25k' (A). Precision controls the number of significant digits after abbreviation. The value 4250.2 is abbreviated to thousands (k), becoming 4.25k with 2 decimal places. It does not display the raw value as 4k (too imprecise), 4.250.2 (invalid), or 4.250.20 (wrong format with padding).

questions.stem: What happens when Collect records is enabled on the Indicator form?

options.text: A preview of the records that match the condition is displayed.
A list of sys_ids is stored during collection to allow drill down to records.
An ad-hoc job runs to collect the scores immediately for testing purposes.
An exact copy of the matching records are retained for future reference.

questions.explanation: When 'Collect records' is enabled on the Indicator form, a list of sys_ids is stored during collection to allow drill down to records (B). This lets users click on a score and see the actual records that contributed to it. It does not show a preview, run an ad-hoc collection job, or retain copies of records. Storing sys_ids enables the Collect Records drill-down feature while keeping storage efficient.

questions.stem:
Consider the following configurations and requirements:
• You plan to set up an Indicator, Average Assignment Duration, to trend the duration of time Resolved Incidents are assigned to Assignment Groups.
• There is an existing metric called Assignment Group which already tracks the duration of time an Incident is assigned to different Assignment Groups.

How would you configure the Indicator Source for the Average Assignment Duration Indicator?

options.text: Facts table: Incident Metric | Conditions: Resolved on Today AND Definition is Assignment Group
Facts table: Incident | Conditions: Resolved on Today AND Value is Assignment Group
Facts table: Incident | Conditions: Resolved on Today AND Definition is Assignment Group
Facts table: Incident Metric | Conditions: Resolved on Today AND Value is Assignment Group

questions.explanation: The Indicator Source should use Facts table: Incident Metric with conditions: Resolved on Today AND Definition is Assignment Group (A). Since the requirement uses an existing metric that tracks assignment group duration, the data is in the Incident Metric table (not the Incident table). 'Definition is Assignment Group' filters for the correct metric type. 'Value' is a numeric field on the metric, not a filter for metric type.

questions.stem:
The formula for % of incidents resolved by first assigned group is configured as follows:

([[ Number of resolved incidents by first assigned group ]] / [[ Number of resolved incidents ]]) * 100

You observe “No Score” whenever the value of Number of resolved incidents component indicator is 0.

What can be done to enhance the formula so it returns 0 instead of “No Score” when there are no resolved incidents?

options.text: Add a conditional JavaScript statement in the formula to return 0 if the value of Number of Resolved Incidents is 0.
Enable the property “Allow formula component to be NULL”.
Set the property “Value when nil” to 0.
Enable the property “Render continuous lines”.

questions.explanation: Add a conditional JavaScript statement in the formula to return 0 when Number of Resolved Incidents is 0 (A). PA formulas support if/else syntax: if ([[Number of resolved incidents]] == 0) {0} else {([[resolved by first assigned group]] / [[resolved incidents]]) * 100}. The properties 'Allow formula component to be NULL' and 'Value when nil' don't address divide-by-zero. 'Render continuous lines' is a display option.

questions.stem: Select the role which can create new Interactive Filters.

options.text: pa_admin
pa_power_user
report_admin
interactive_filter_user

questions.explanation: The pa_admin role can create new Interactive Filters. Interactive Filters are an administrative PA feature that requires the PA Admin role to create and manage. pa_power_user can use existing filters but not create new ones. report_admin manages reports, not PA interactive filters. interactive_filter_user is not a standard ServiceNow role. PA Admin has full control over all PA configuration including interactive filters.

questions.stem: As a good practice, Historical Collection should be configured to run:

options.text: Weekly
Daily
Monthly
Once or On Demand

questions.explanation: Historical Collection should be configured to run Once or On Demand (D) as a best practice. Historical data collection reconstructs past scores and only needs to run once to backfill data. Running it daily, weekly, or monthly wastes resources because historical scores don't change once collected. After the initial historical collection run, ongoing data is captured by the regular daily/weekly collection jobs.

questions.stem: When is a script required to perform a Breakdown Mapping for a Breakdown based on a Bucket group?

options.text: When there is no field in the indicator Facts table that matches the value to be bucketed
When mapping to a Manual Indicator
When needing to limit the visibility of the Buckets
When the Breakdown is a Manual Breakdown

questions.explanation: A script is required for Breakdown Mapping with a Bucket group when there is no field in the indicator Facts table that matches the value to be bucketed (A). Bucket groups recategorize values into ranges, but if the source field isn't directly available on the facts table, a script must extract or calculate the value before bucketing. Manual Indicators (B), visibility limits (C), and Manual Breakdowns (D) don't specifically require scripted bucket mappings.

questions.stem: When using Text Analytics in Performance Analytics, what fields are analyzed?

options.text: All Journal fields on all records
All String fields on all records
Configured String fields from Indicator sources that have scores collected
Short (less than 100 characters) String fields on all records

questions.explanation: Text Analytics in PA analyzes configured String fields from Indicator sources that have scores collected (C). Text Analytics only processes fields that have been specifically configured for analysis and only for indicators with active collection. It does not analyze all journal fields, all string fields, or only short string fields. The administrator selects which string fields to include in the text analytics configuration.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Show multiple elements as property of a widget?

options.text: Apply an Element filter to Breakdown element trends
Control the presentation of multiple element trends
Enable Multi-element select on a Breakdown Dashboard
Allow a widget to follow a Breakdown source

questions.explanation: The 'Show multiple elements as' property of a widget controls the presentation of multiple element trends (B). It determines how multiple breakdown elements are displayed together, such as stacked, grouped, or overlaid. It does not apply element filters (A), enable multi-element selection on dashboards (C), or make widgets follow breakdown sources (D). It is a display configuration option for multi-element visualizations.

questions.stem: When configuring a Breakdown Source on a Dashboard, how do you ensure that Performance Analytics widgets are filtered correctly?

options.text: Edit each widget and enable “Apply Dashboard Filter”
For each widget, enable “Follow interactive filter”
Edit each widget and enable “Follow element”
For each widget, enable “Act as interactive filter”

questions.explanation: When configuring a Breakdown Source on a Dashboard, to ensure PA widgets are filtered correctly, edit each widget and enable 'Follow element' (C). This setting makes the widget respond to the selected breakdown element from the dashboard breakdown source. 'Apply Dashboard Filter' (A) and 'Follow interactive filter' (B) relate to interactive filters, not breakdown sources. 'Act as interactive filter' (D) makes a widget emit events, not receive them.

questions.stem: How many levels of Breakdowns are available if Collect breakdown matrix is NOT checked on the Indicator?

options.text: 0 - This must be checked to collect Breakdowns.
There is no limit on the levels of Breakdowns collected.
2 - Two levels of Breakdowns are always collected.
1 - Without the matrix, a single level of Breakdowns is collected.

questions.explanation: Without 'Collect breakdown matrix' checked, only 1 level of Breakdowns is collected (D). Single-level means scores are collected for each breakdown independently but not for combinations of breakdowns. With the matrix enabled, multi-level combinations (cross-breakdowns) are collected, creating exponentially more scores. The checkbox does not affect whether breakdowns are collected at all (A is wrong), and there is a practical limit (B is wrong).
